primary_claim: A compact ~8-10 dimensional manifold extracted from scGPT's attention heads, encoding hematopoietic differentiation progression, can be extracted as a standalone algorithm (frozen attention weights plus a lightweight adaptor and readout head) that significantly outperforms established single-cell bioinformatics methods (scVI, Palantir, Diffusion Pseudotime, CellTypist, PCA, raw-expression) on pseudotime-depth ordering and leads on several classification tasks, while being compressible to a single attention head (5.9 MB) or a rank-64 SVD surrogate (0.73 MB) with only modest performance loss.

effect.metric: pseudotime-depth ordering and classification performance vs. established methods; compression size vs. performance retention
effect.value: extracted algorithm significantly outperforms all tested alternatives on pseudotime-depth ordering (paired split-level statistics); extracted 10-dim head beats a 175K-parameter MLP baseline on 6/8 classification endpoints while being 34.5x faster and ~1000x fewer parameters; rank-64 SVD surrogate (0.73MB) still beats the MLP baseline on all 8 endpoints

stated_future_work: Apply these methods to other biological systems and developmental processes
Develop better unsupervised techniques for manifold discovery that scale beyond the current semi-supervised approach
limitations_stated: On some stage-level and branch-level macro-F1 classification metrics, diffusion-style baselines or raw expression had the edge, so results are not a clean sweep
Rank-64 SVD compression incurs statistically significant losses versus the dense single-head operator on 5 of 8 endpoints
Mechanistic interpretability methods like this are dual-use and could enable capability amplification if applied to large language models
quote: the extracted algorithm appeared to be the best, significantly outperforming every tested alternative in paired split-level statistics
